title: How to cope with climate anxiety, with Thomas Doherty, PsyD, and Ashlee Cunsolo, PhD

sentences.en: Over the past several years, climate change has moved from an abstract idea to a reality in many of our lives.
sentences.zh: 过去几年里，气候变化已从一个抽象的概念，变成了我们许多人生活中的现实。

sentences.en: A reality that has a lot of us increasingly worried.
sentences.zh: 一个让许多人日益感到担忧的现实。

sentences.en: An APA survey in February 2020 found that two-thirds of American adults said that they felt at least a little eco-anxiety,
sentences.zh: 美国心理学会（APA）在2020年2月的一项调查发现，三分之二的美国成年人表示他们至少感到了一点“生态焦虑”，

sentences.en: which is defined as worry or concern about climate change and its effects.
sentences.zh: 即对气候变化及其影响的担忧或关切。

sentences.en: And nearly half of those under age 34 said that stress about climate change affects their daily lives.
sentences.zh: 而在34岁以下的人群中，近一半人表示对气候变化的压力影响了他们的日常生活。

sentences.en: Since then, hurricanes in the south, wildfires in the west, and an unprecedented ice storm in Texas
sentences.zh: 从那时起，南部的飓风、西部的野火以及德克萨斯州史无前例的冰暴，

sentences.en: have kept climate change in our thoughts this year, even as COVID-19 has dominated the headlines.
sentences.zh: 即使在新冠疫情占据新闻头条的情况下，也让气候变化在今年始终萦绕在我们的心头。

sentences.en: So what are the mental health effects of climate change?
sentences.zh: 那么，气候变化对心理健康有什么影响呢？

sentences.en: Who is most at risk of suffering eco-anxiety?
sentences.zh: 谁最容易受到生态焦虑的困扰？

sentences.en: What is ecological grief?
sentences.zh: 什么是生态悲伤？

sentences.en: And what can we do to cope and build resilience in ourselves when prospects for the future of the planet seem so bleak?
sentences.zh: 当地球的未来前景看起来如此黯淡时，我们该如何应对并建立心理韧性？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们有两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Thomas Doherty, a clinical and environmental psychologist in Portland, Oregon,
sentences.zh: 第一位是托马斯·多尔蒂博士，他是俄勒冈州波特兰市的一位临床和环境心理学家，

sentences.en: who studies nature-based therapies, that is, the restorative effects of outdoor experience and the mental health impacts of climate change.
sentences.zh: 他研究基于自然的疗法，即户外体验的修复作用以及气候变化对心理健康的影响。

sentences.en: His 2011 paper, The Psychological Impacts of Global Climate Change, has been cited by other researchers more than 500 times.
sentences.zh: 他2011年的论文《全球气候变化的心理影响》已被其他研究人员引用超过500次。

sentences.en: He's a fellow of APA, a contributor to the association's 2017 report, Mental Health and
sentences.zh: 他是美国心理学会的会士，也是该协会2017年报告《心理健康与

sentences.en: Our Changing Climate, and a founding editor of the journal Ecopsychology.
sentences.zh: 我们不断变化的气候》的撰稿人，还是《生态心理学》期刊的创始编辑。

sentences.en: Also with us is Dr. Ashley Consolo, founding dean of the School of Arctic and Subarctic Studies at the Labrador Institute of Memorial University in Newfoundland, Canada.
sentences.zh: 另一位嘉宾是阿什利·康索洛博士，她是加拿大纽芬兰纪念大学拉布拉多研究所北极与亚北极研究学院的创始院长。

sentences.en: Dr. Consolo is a public health researcher who has spent more than a decade studying how climate
sentences.zh: 康索洛博士是一位公共卫生研究员，她花了十多年时间研究气候

sentences.en: change and environmental losses are affecting the mental health of the indigenous Inuit community
sentences.zh: 变化和环境损失如何影响加拿大原住民因纽特社区的心理健康，

sentences.en: in Canada, as well as developing programs to help the community deal with those losses.
sentences.zh: 并致力于开发项目以帮助该社区应对这些损失。

sentences.en: With other researchers, she coined the term ecological grief to describe the grief people feel at environmental loss, including loss caused by climate change.
sentences.zh: 她与其他研究人员共同创造了“生态悲伤”一词，用来描述人们因环境损失（包括气候变化造成的损失）而感到的悲伤。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 感谢两位今天加入我们的节目。

sentences.en: Welcome.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你们。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: It's great to be here, Kim.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，金。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Doherty, let's start with you.
sentences.zh: 那么，多尔蒂博士，我们先从您开始。

sentences.en: Those numbers I cited in the introduction from APA survey last year were very high.
sentences.zh: 我在介绍中引用的去年美国心理学会调查的数据非常高。

sentences.en: More than two-thirds of Americans said that they feel some eco-anxiety.
sentences.zh: 超过三分之二的美国人表示他们感到了一些生态焦虑。

sentences.en: And a number I didn't mention is that more than half of respondents said they felt that climate change was the biggest issue facing society today.
sentences.zh: 还有一个我没提到的数字是，超过一半的受访者表示他们认为气候变化是当今社会面临的最大问题。

sentences.en: As a clinician and practicing psychologist, does this ring true for you?
sentences.zh: 作为一名临床医生和执业心理学家，这符合您的观察吗？

sentences.en: Is this something that you're seeing in your practice?
sentences.zh: 这是您在执业中观察到的情况吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it does, Kim.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此，金。

sentences.en: It does ring true.
sentences.zh: 这确实符合事实。

sentences.en: I mean, those numbers are kind of sobering, but I'm really not surprised.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些数字令人清醒，但我一点也不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I've known of Ashley's work and we've been in contact for many years.
sentences.zh: 我了解阿什利的工作，我们已经联系多年了。

sentences.en: Maybe it may be as much as a decade and, you know, things were different when we first started corresponding in terms of the distance of climate change and the abstract nature of
sentences.zh: 可能长达十年之久，你知道，当我们刚开始通信时，情况有所不同，就气候变化的距离感和抽象性而言，

sentences.en: it.
sentences.zh: 它（当时）还是抽象的。

sentences.en: But that really has changed.
sentences.zh: 但现在确实变了。

sentences.en: We knew that was going to change.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它会改变。

sentences.en: That was what the predictions of scientists, atmospheric scientists were, but it has changed.
sentences.zh: 这就是科学家、大气科学家们的预测，但它确实已经改变了。

sentences.en: So, people do have direct experience of climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们确实对气候变化有了直接的体验。

sentences.en: And I do think when we're talking about issues like eco-anxiety or eco-grief, we're talking about at least two things.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为，当我们谈论生态焦虑或生态悲伤这类问题时，我们至少在谈论两件事。

sentences.en: One is more of a sociological, cultural-wide reckoning with this issue, climate change, much like we reckoned with, say, the nuclear war in the 1950s and 60s.
sentences.zh: 一是更广泛的社会学和文化层面对气候变化这一问题的清算，就像我们在20世纪50年代和60年代对核战争的清算一样。

sentences.en: And it was a big cultural debate and it was a very troubling politicized issue.
sentences.zh: 那是一场重大的文化辩论，也是一个非常令人不安的政治化议题。

sentences.en: And same with climate change.
sentences.zh: 气候变化也是如此。

sentences.en: People have, it is normal to be anxious about climate change.
sentences.zh: 人们对气候变化感到焦虑是很正常的。

sentences.en: And then also, as a clinician, I start to think about people's functioning and then we get
sentences.zh: 此外，作为一名临床医生，我开始考虑人们的功能，然后我们进入了

sentences.en: into the realm of disorders and anxiety disorders, depression disorders, and there's a spectrum
sentences.zh: 障碍领域，如焦虑症、抑郁症，这里有一个从

sentences.en: from, you know, healthy adjustments to stressors to adjustment disorders and then diagnosable issues.
sentences.zh: 对压力源的健康适应，到适应障碍，再到可诊断问题的光谱。

sentences.en: So, I think, you know, when we get into this topic, it's helpful to, it's helpful to make sure that we realize there's a number of ways to think about eco-anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为，当我们探讨这个话题时，确保我们意识到思考生态焦虑有多种方式是很有帮助的。

sentences.en: Dr. Consol, you're not a practitioner, but are you experiencing the same kinds of reactions from the people you work with?
sentences.zh: 康索洛博士，您不是临床医生，但您在与您共事的人群中是否也感受到了同样的反应？

sentences.en: Yeah, certainly.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: I mean, I think in the research that I'm doing and with people who are on the ground and particularly
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为在我所做的研究中，以及与那些身处一线的人们，特别是

sentences.en: people living in Northern Canada who are at the front lines of a rapidly changing climate, this is something that people are experiencing directly.
sentences.zh: 生活在加拿大北部、处于气候快速变化前线的人们接触时，这是人们直接经历的事情。

sentences.en: It's something they've been living with and adapting to for decades.
sentences.zh: 这是他们几十年来一直生活并适应的事情。

sentences.en: It's something that has been a mental health stressor, both directly creating new stressors,
sentences.zh: 它一直是一个心理健康压力源，既直接创造了新的压力，

sentences.en: but also magnifying other underlying mental health conditions or mental health challenges.
sentences.zh: 也放大了其他潜在的心理健康状况或心理健康挑战。

sentences.en: And it's something that you're really seeing, like research is focusing on it more and more.
sentences.zh: 而且你确实能看到，研究正越来越多地关注它。

sentences.en: I'm getting contacted more and more by interested grad students, which is really exciting.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的感兴趣的研究生联系我，这真的很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: You know, people see the importance of this and want to go into this field now, which, you know, as Thomas mentioned, when we first started corresponding 10 years ago, it wasn't,
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们看到了这一点的重要性，现在想进入这个领域，正如托马斯提到的，当我们10年前刚开始通信时，它还不是，

sentences.en: it was a new area.
sentences.zh: 它是一个新的领域。

sentences.en: It was something new people were considering.
sentences.zh: 这是人们当时正在考虑的新事物。

sentences.en: And now we're seeing it as an emergence of a very important pressing field that more and more research is going into, more and more research funding and more and more interests.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我们看到它作为一个非常重要、紧迫的领域正在兴起，越来越多的研究投入其中，越来越多的研究资金和越来越多的兴趣。

sentences.en: And I think also in the kind of public conversation and dialogue and debate, we're seeing a lot of
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在公共对话和辩论中，我们也看到了很多

sentences.en: discussion in the media and a lot of focus around eco-anxiety, eco-grief, how people are experiencing this and choosing to narrate their own sort of self-reported experiences.
sentences.zh: 媒体讨论，以及对生态焦虑、生态悲伤的极大关注，人们如何经历这些，并选择叙述他们自己报告的经历。

sentences.en: So, you know, as Thomas said, those numbers from the APA survey are sobering, but not surprising.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如托马斯所说，美国心理学会调查的那些数字令人清醒，但并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And I think it's great that we're starting to get a broader understanding of the prevalence and the distribution of how many people are actually being affected to various degrees
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，我们开始更广泛地了解有多少人实际上在不同程度上受到气候变化的影响，

sentences.en: by climate change and on their mental health.
sentences.zh: 以及这对他们的心理健康有何影响，这非常好。

sentences.en: In a 2017 report, APA and the climate nonprofit group EcoAmerica actually came up with the term eco-anxiety and defined it as chronic fear of environmental doom.
sentences.zh: 在2017年的一份报告中，美国心理学会和气候非营利组织EcoAmerica实际上提出了“生态焦虑”一词，并将其定义为对环境末日的慢性恐惧。

sentences.en: And while the term has caught on, it's not a clinical diagnosis, but how do psychologists think about defining and recognizing and ultimately treating eco-anxiety?
sentences.zh: 虽然这个词已经流行起来，但它不是一个临床诊断，那么心理学家是如何定义、识别并最终治疗生态焦虑的呢？

sentences.en: It's a real thing, right?
sentences.zh: 这是真实存在的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, as I said, I mean, again, psychology is a broad field.
sentences.zh: 是的，正如我所说，心理学是一个广泛的领域。

sentences.en: We have colleagues and Ashley and other folks that we know, we're studying this on a cultural
sentences.zh: 我们有同事，还有阿什利和其他我们认识的人，我们正在从文化层面研究这个问题，

sentences.en: level, you know, what people's basic identity, their values, their sense of themselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们的基本身份、价值观、自我意识。

sentences.en: You know, I use the term environmental identity a lot, and that's an important construct here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我经常使用“环境身份”这个词，这是这里的一个重要概念。

sentences.en: People have a sense of their identity in relation to nature and the natural world, much like their cultural identity or their gender identity or their ethnic identity.
sentences.zh: 人们对自己在自然和自然世界中的身份有一种认同感，就像他们的文化身份、性别身份或民族身份一样。

sentences.en: People are being, you know, their consciousness is being raised about their environmental identity with issues like climate change.
sentences.zh: 人们的意识正在被唤醒，关于他们与气候变化等问题的环境身份。

sentences.en: Obviously, you know, First Nations people in the Arctic and indigenous people have a very well-developed sense of environmental identity based on their culture and their values and
sentences.zh: 显然，北极的原住民和土著人民基于他们的文化、价值观和

sentences.en: their spirituality.
sentences.zh: 灵性，有着非常成熟的环境身份感。

sentences.en: But people in the sort of regular world also have various kinds of environmental identities.
sentences.zh: 但普通世界的人们也有各种各样的环境身份。

sentences.en: And so when we, it's a healthy way to start talking about this concept, this topic of environmental anxiety, we get anxious or we have grief because we have things that we
sentences.zh: 所以当我们开始谈论环境焦虑这个概念时，这是一种健康的开始方式，我们感到焦虑或悲伤，是因为我们有

sentences.en: value are threatened, you know, our self, either personally or things that we value are threatened or we witness this, and then it causes us to have these emotions.
sentences.zh: 重视的东西受到了威胁，无论是我们个人，还是我们重视的事物受到了威胁，或者我们目睹了这一切，这导致我们产生了这些情绪。

sentences.en: Dr. Consolo, in your work, you do talk a lot about ecological grief.
sentences.zh: 康索洛博士，在您的工作中，您确实谈了很多关于生态悲伤的问题。

sentences.en: How does that relate to eco-anxiety?
sentences.zh: 这与生态焦虑有什么关系？

sentences.en: And where do the two terms overlap and how are they different?
sentences.zh: 这两个术语在哪里重叠，又有什么不同？

sentences.en: I think they overlap in a great way.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们在很大程度上是重叠的。

sentences.en: You know, the anxiety that people feel, as Thomas just said, is related to the things that they're worried about losing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如托马斯刚才所说，人们感到的焦虑与他们担心失去的东西有关。

sentences.en: So whether it's their environmental identity or their cultural or their social identity or things that are important to them in their lives or in the case of very acute things like
sentences.zh: 所以无论是他们的环境身份、文化或社会身份，还是他们生活中重要的事物，或者在野火或洪水等非常突发的情况下，即实际的破坏和损失，都有与之相关的焦虑，以及围绕预知未来而产生的焦虑。

sentences.en: wildfires or flooding where it's actual destruction and loss, there's anxiety related to that and related to future thinking around knowing what's to come.
sentences.zh: 而且还有相关的悲伤。

sentences.en: And then there's also the associated grief.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，至少在我自己的研究中看到的，以及人们在媒体报道中指出的，或者我们看到的纪录片和其他表达形式中，

sentences.en: And for a lot of people, at least what I'm seeing in my own research and what people are identifying in, say, you know, media reports or we're seeing documentaries and other forms
sentences.zh: 焦虑和悲伤正开始携手并进。

sentences.en: of expression, anxiety and grief are starting to go hand in hand.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对变化感到焦虑，然后他们既为可能正在经历的当前变化感到悲伤，也为可能即将到来的未来损失感到悲伤。

sentences.en: So people are feeling anxious about the changes and then they're grieving both the current changes that they might be experiencing or the future loss that might be coming.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种同时存在焦虑和悲伤的当前时间体验。

sentences.en: So there's this current temporal experience of both anxiety and grief.
sentences.zh: 然后还有这种对未来的恐惧。

sentences.en: And then there's also this future fear.
sentences.zh: 许多人谈论哀悼即将发生的事情。

sentences.en: And a lot of people talk about mourning what's to come.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常迷人的部分，当我们思考人们每天经历什么样的压力源时，我们需要努力解决这个问题，

sentences.en: And I think this is a really fascinating piece that we need to grapple with when we're thinking
sentences.zh: 因为有时最大的压力来自未来和对未来的预期。

sentences.en: about what type of stressors people are experiencing daily, because sometimes the biggest stresses are coming from future and anticipating future.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，悲伤是失去的部分，当我们知道失去了什么时所经历的痛苦，因为我们只会为我们所爱的东西悲伤。

sentences.en: So for me, the grief is the peace that's lost and the pain that's experienced when we know what's lost, because we only grieve what we love.
sentences.zh: 当我们失去所爱之物时，就会有哀悼和悲伤的行为。

sentences.en: And when we lose something that we love, there's that act of mourning and grief.
sentences.zh: 而焦虑是其中的一部分，因为你可以在悲伤之前、期间和之后感到焦虑。

sentences.en: And the anxiety is a part of that, because you can have anxiety before the grief, during and after.
sentences.zh: 所以它们是非常紧密相连的。

sentences.en: So they're very interlinked.
sentences.zh: 而且它们确实是人们经常一起表达的东西。

sentences.en: And they're certainly something that people often articulate together.
sentences.zh: 我在自己的研究中发现，人们会谈论焦虑，然后开始谈论这种焦虑如何指向他们所恐惧的未来悲伤。

sentences.en: And I found in my own research, you know, people will talk about anxiety and then start to talk about how that anxiety points to future grief that they're afraid of.
sentences.zh: 所以即使他们还没有达到悲伤阶段，他们也在某种程度上将两者联系起来。

sentences.en: So they're kind of linking even if they haven't hit the grief stage yet.
sentences.zh: 我可以建议可能还有其他尚未被创造出来的术语吗？

sentences.en: Can I suggest that there might be other terms out there that maybe haven't been coined yet?
sentences.zh: 虽然围绕这一现象已经有了很多语言。

sentences.en: Although there's a lot of language that's growing up around this whole phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 但我一直在思考“生态疲惫”或“生态顺从”，这是一种人们在听到又一个无法解决的危机时可能会产生的感觉。

sentences.en: But I was thinking about eco-exhaustion or eco-resignation, kind of a feeling that people might get by hearing about yet another crisis about which you can't do anything.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚毁灭性的火灾，格陵兰岛融化的冰盖，似乎每天都有关于全球某个地区被气候变化蹂躏的新闻。

sentences.en: The devastating fires in Australia, the melting ice pack in Greenland, it seems that every day there's another story about some part of the globe that is being wracked by climate
sentences.zh: 所以您有时会感到，您从共事的人那里听到希望破灭了吗？

sentences.en: change.
sentences.zh: 是的，在这种情况下我使用的术语是“气候人质”。

sentences.en: So do you sometimes feel, do you hear from people you work with that hope is lost?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们觉得我们像是这个更大过程的人质。

sentences.en: Yeah, the term that I use in that case is what I call a climate hostage.
sentences.zh: 这是事实，因为普通公民没有太多权力去指导政府或企业来解决气候问题。

sentences.en: You know, we feel like we're kind of hostages to this larger process.

sentences.en: I mean, and so we have young people, you know, trying to work through legal to the courts, you know, so yeah, that is one angle here.
sentences.zh: 我是说，所以我们有年轻人，你知道，试图通过法律途径诉诸法庭，所以是的，这是一个切入点。

sentences.en: There are, there are, there is climate injustice.
sentences.zh: 这里存在，存在，存在气候不公正。

sentences.en: There are people that have legitimately stymied, you know, healthy action on climate change.
sentences.zh: 有些人确实阻碍了，你知道，针对气候变化采取健康的行动。

sentences.en: We've been able to take action on things like chlorofluorocarbons or removing lead from gasoline and many other really difficult, you know, processes have, have been able to
sentences.zh: 我们已经能够对诸如氯氟烃或从汽油中去除铅等问题采取行动，许多其他非常困难的，你知道，过程也已经

sentences.en: happen, but climate change has been politicized and stymied.
sentences.zh: 得以实现，但气候变化却被政治化和阻碍了。

sentences.en: So that, that, that anger that people feel is, is legitimate, but it's just one of many emotions.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们感受到的那种愤怒是，是合情合理的，但这只是众多情绪中的一种。

sentences.en: And so we, you know, I, one of the many images I use with people is, you know, the idea of
sentences.zh: 所以我们，你知道，我，我与人们交流时使用的众多意象之一，你知道，就是

sentences.en: a compass and a compass will point, you know, the needle will point north as you walk around and it'll move freely.
sentences.zh: 指南针的概念，指南针会指向，你知道，当你走动时指针会指向北方，它可以自由转动。

sentences.en: So we want to have our emotions to be able to move freely.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望我们的情绪也能自由流动。

sentences.en: I will feel anger, but I also can feel hope.
sentences.zh: 我会感到愤怒，但我也可以感到希望。

sentences.en: I can also feel happiness.
sentences.zh: 我也可以感到快乐。

sentences.en: I can feel calmness.
sentences.zh: 我可以感到平静。

sentences.en: And so some of this, again, is emotional intelligence, basic psychology stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以这其中一些，再次强调，是关于情商，基础心理学的东西。

sentences.en: How do we, how do we feel a range of emotions?
sentences.zh: 我们如何，我们如何感受一系列的情绪？

sentences.en: How do we, how, how can we be in the present moment?
sentences.zh: 我们如何，我们如何才能活在当下？

sentences.en: How do we do our own mental hygiene?
sentences.zh: 我们如何进行自己的心理卫生保健？

sentences.en: You know, and young people do, you know, you know, do well with mentoring about this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，年轻人，你知道，在接受这类事情的指导方面做得很好。

sentences.en: You know, so there's a lot of ways that we can prevent more.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以有很多方法可以预防更多的问题。

sentences.en: Or we can, we can help to direct the anger in a healthy, growthful way versus into a way of despair, jadedness, you know, self-hate, you know, the world might be a problem, but
sentences.zh: 或者我们可以，我们可以帮助以一种健康、成长的方式引导愤怒，而不是陷入绝望、厌世，你知道，自我厌恶，你知道，世界可能是一个问题，但

sentences.en: it doesn't mean you are a problem.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你是一个问题。

sentences.en: So again, there's that blame.
sentences.zh: 所以再次强调，这里存在指责的问题。

sentences.en: There's a blame issue that we have to be careful about here, that people somehow think climate change is my, it's my fault.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个我们必须小心的指责问题，即人们不知何故认为气候变化是我的，是我的错。

sentences.en: And part of that is, is been the misinformation that, you know, this has been put on individual people versus, you know, systems of power and incorporation.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是，一直以来的虚假信息，你知道，这被归咎于个人，而不是，你知道，权力体系和企业。

sentences.en: So there's a whole political critical piece here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一个完整的政治批判层面。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Consolo, you're in Canada.
sentences.zh: 那么，康索洛博士，你在加拿大。

sentences.en: I'm just wondering, do you have the same sense of anti-science and climate change denial that we have in the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道，你是否也像我们在美国一样，感受到同样的反科学和气候变化否认论？

sentences.en: What is it like there?
sentences.zh: 那里情况如何？

sentences.en: I don't think it's to the extent that we've certainly seen come out of the U.S., particularly over the last four years.
sentences.zh: 我不认为达到了我们从美国看到的那种程度，特别是在过去四年里。

sentences.en: But we, we definitely do have it.
sentences.zh: 但我们，我们确实也有这种情况。

sentences.en: And I, I don't think that Canada by any means is a, is a place that is, you know, has clean hands in the climate misinformation.
sentences.zh: 而且我，我不认为加拿大在任何方面是一个，是一个，你知道，在气候虚假信息方面清白的地方。

sentences.en: You know, we've, we've gone through a number of things where governments have had different policies and haven't supported climate initiatives.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们经历过一些政府有不同政策且不支持气候倡议的事情。

sentences.en: And I think this is something that is a global political reckoning.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个全球性的政治清算。

sentences.en: I absolutely agree with Thomas.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意托马斯的观点。

sentences.en: This is something people have known about for decades and the science has been clear for decades.
sentences.zh: 这是人们几十年来一直都知道的事情，科学界几十年来也一直很明确。

sentences.en: But there hasn't been a will to globally act for, you know, a whole variety of reasons.
sentences.zh: 但出于各种各样的原因，全球范围内一直缺乏采取行动的意愿。

sentences.en: So I, I, I do think it's something that people, that anger is legitimate about.
sentences.zh: 所以我，我，我确实认为这是人们，那种愤怒是合情合理的。

sentences.en: I know that I go through bouts where I feel angry, but then for, for me and, and, you know, speaking personally, the, the anger is exhausting and it's not sustainable for me.
sentences.zh: 我知道我也会经历感到愤怒的时期，但对我来说，而且，你知道，就我个人而言，愤怒是令人精疲力竭的，对我来说是不可持续的。

sentences.en: So I have to find those other places to go to.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须找到其他可以去的地方。

sentences.en: And I love that imagery of the compass, Thomas.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢那个指南针的意象，托马斯。

sentences.en: I think that's, that's just great because how do you hold the anger, but move to the other things that are more productive, more positive that for, for me personally, anger
sentences.zh: 我觉得那，那真是太棒了，因为你如何保持愤怒，同时转向其他更具建设性、更积极的事情，对我个人而言，愤怒

sentences.en: often debilitates.
sentences.zh: 往往会让人变得虚弱。

sentences.en: So I have to find ways to move into the other, the other pieces.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须找到方法转向其他，其他的方面。

sentences.en: Um, and I think I, you know, I, I hear a lot of young people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我，你知道，我，我听到了很多年轻人的声音。

sentences.en: I know my, my own 16 year old will sometimes say, you know, your generation and, you know,
sentences.zh: 我知道我，我自己的16岁孩子有时会说，你知道，你们这一代，还有，你知道，

sentences.en: grandparents generation, you, you really left us in a crisis, you know, and, and, and it's true, you know, and, and, and generations before, and we have a lot of reckoning.
sentences.zh: 祖辈那一代，你们，你们真的把我们留在了危机中，你知道，而且，而且，这是真的，你知道，而且，之前的几代人也是，我们有很多需要清算的。

sentences.en: And I think it's something we can't leave to young people.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们不能留给年轻人的事情。

sentences.en: And I think there's sometimes a sense that we're just going to leave it to the next generation.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有时有一种感觉，就是我们只是要把问题留给下一代。

sentences.en: I think it's something that all generations need to work together, but I think anger is something we need to support.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是所有世代都需要共同努力的事情，但我认为愤怒是我们确实需要支持的东西。

sentences.en: And that's, that's where people like Thomas and other mental health professionals come in to provide that, that mentoring support so people can work through and understand their
sentences.zh: 这就是，这就是像托马斯和其他心理健康专业人士发挥作用的地方，提供那种，那种指导支持，这样人们就可以理清并理解他们的

sentences.en: experiences are legitimate, but how do they express them in positive, productive, healthy ways that won't, won't harm themselves in the future.
sentences.zh: 经历是合情合理的，但他们如何以积极、建设性、健康的方式表达出来，而不会在未来伤害到自己。

sentences.en: What kinds of changes are you both seeing in psychological science with respect to climate change?
sentences.zh: 你们两位在心理科学领域看到了哪些关于气候变化的变化？

sentences.en: Is this becoming much more of an accepted area of, of research and scholarship?
sentences.zh: 这是否正在成为一个被广泛接受的研究和学术领域？

sentences.en: I think from a research and scholarship perspective, we're seeing a lot, you know, there's just so much more coming online.
sentences.zh: 我认为从研究和学术的角度来看，我们看到了很多，你知道，只是有更多相关内容上线了。

sentences.en: And so, so much, people are really starting to look at it from multiple perspectives, which
sentences.zh: 所以，这么多，人们真的开始从多个角度来看待它，这

sentences.en: is really exciting to see, you know, we're seeing the, the longitudinal studies, we're seeing
sentences.zh: 真的很令人兴奋，你知道，我们看到了，纵向研究，我们看到了

sentences.en: case studies, we're seeing mixed methods, we're seeing population level, we're seeing the very clinical, the very social cultural piece, like it's, it's a very diverse field right
sentences.zh: 案例研究，我们看到了混合方法，我们看到了人口层面，我们看到了非常临床的、非常社会文化的层面，就像它，它是一个非常多元化的领域

sentences.en: now.
sentences.zh: 现在。

sentences.en: But in many ways, it's still quite new.
sentences.zh: 但在许多方面，它仍然相当新。

sentences.en: And I think that people's lived experiences with the mental health impacts of climate change really outstrip what we actually know.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们对气候变化带来的心理健康影响的亲身经历，确实超出了我们目前所知的范围。

sentences.en: And I think that that's one of the huge challenges and, and often sometimes the failings of our field is we're not keeping up with what people are actually experiencing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是巨大的挑战之一，而且往往有时是我们领域的失败之处，因为我们没有跟上人们实际经历的事情。

sentences.en: And so there's so many unanswered questions, but people are already suffering around the globe.
sentences.zh: 所以有太多未解的问题，但全球各地的人们已经在受苦了。

sentences.en: So how we, how we act quickly without needing to do more research, but also having the research to back up the actions is, is the real dilemma we're facing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们如何在不需要做更多研究的情况下迅速采取行动，同时又拥有支持这些行动的研究，是我们面临的真正困境。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think there's a consilience here in the sense that people that have been working on disasters,
sentences.zh: 我认为这里有一种共识，即那些一直致力于灾害研究的人们，

sentences.en: disaster intervention that traditionally would work on fires and floods, that is now wrapping in more into the larger climate change, climate change world.
sentences.zh: 传统上用于应对火灾和洪水的灾害干预，现在正越来越多地被纳入到更广泛的气候变化领域中。

sentences.en: And then, especially recently, social justice, social justice issues.
sentences.zh: 尤其是最近，社会正义问题也涵盖在内。

sentences.en: Now, you know, most climate active activism groups think of themselves as environmental justice groups.
sentences.zh: 现在，大多数气候行动组织都将自己视为环境正义组织。

sentences.en: So we have a, we have a blending of the disaster work and the, and the more office-based clinical
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将灾害应对工作与那种基于办公室的临床工作融合在了一起，

sentences.en: work dealing with the stress and the anxiety from a distance and the social justice work.
sentences.zh: 这种临床工作旨在远程处理压力和焦虑，同时也涉及社会正义工作。

sentences.en: And, uh, many people are self, self-motivating.
sentences.zh: 而且，许多人都有自我激励的动力。

sentences.en: They're, they're, again, they're getting ahead of the academy is actually saying, and they're practitioners are starting to work on this.
sentences.zh: 他们再次走在了学术界的前面，实际上，从业者们已经开始着手处理这些问题了。

sentences.en: And my goal is to try to knit this together in a, in a really, you know, a comprehensive way.
sentences.zh: 我的目标是尝试以一种真正全面的方式将这些内容整合在一起。

sentences.en: So we don't have to reinvent the wheel.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就不必重复造轮子了。

sentences.en: That's the, that's the thing I've noticed, you know, you know, people come into this field, they don't realize that people have been working on this for many, many years.
sentences.zh: 这就是我注意到的情况，人们进入这个领域时，并没有意识到其实已经有很多人为此工作了许多年。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, I think that's the challenge for psychology is how to get the, how to get all the stories together.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对心理学界来说是一个挑战，即如何将所有的经验和故事汇集起来。

sentences.en: So we don't, we're not in separate silos.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就不会各自为政，处于孤立的状态。

sentences.en: What are the questions that we still need to answer about the mental health effects of climate change?
sentences.zh: 关于气候变化对心理健康的影响，我们还有哪些问题需要解答？

sentences.en: What, what are you both studying now?
sentences.zh: 你们两位现在都在研究什么？

sentences.en: Uh, there's so much, you know, and, and we can't individually study at all, but there is, there's so much we don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有太多东西了，我们无法独自研究所有问题，但确实还有很多我们未知的东西。

sentences.en: Um, I'm particularly interested right now, I'm working with a team in Canada to look at a study on the prevalence and distribution at the population level for Canada of the, of
sentences.zh: 我目前特别感兴趣的是，我正在与加拿大的一支团队合作，进行一项关于加拿大人口层面生态焦虑、生态悲伤以及其他心理健康结果的患病率和分布的研究，

sentences.en: eco-anxiety and eco-grief and other mental health, um, outcomes, because we don't have a population level study in Canada.
sentences.zh: 因为在加拿大，我们还没有进行过人口层面的研究。

sentences.en: Uh, and what we're running up against is when we talk to policymakers and decision makers,
sentences.zh: 我们遇到的困难是，当我们与政策制定者和决策者交谈时，

sentences.en: they'll say, well, it's great that there's all this, you know, research from other places, or you have these case studies, but what are we actually looking at?
sentences.zh: 他们会说，很高兴有来自其他地方的研究，或者有这些案例研究，但我们到底在面对什么？

sentences.en: So something in the way that the APA did, where you can say, okay, two thirds of people living in Canada express this, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们需要像美国心理学会（APA）那样做一些研究，这样你就可以说，好吧，加拿大有三分之二的人表达了这种感受，明白吗？

sentences.en: So, so that's something that I think is key, particularly from our, our country perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这非常关键，特别是从我们国家的角度来看。

sentences.en: Um, but I'm also particularly interested in those intersections that Thomas highlighted, like the, the social and climate justice, the mental health pieces, what we already know,
sentences.zh: 但我对托马斯强调的那些交叉领域也特别感兴趣，比如社会正义与气候正义、心理健康部分，以及我们已经了解的内容，

sentences.en: um, and looking at some of the key projections.
sentences.zh: 同时也在关注一些关键的预测数据。

sentences.en: So there's very little research right now that looks at, um, putting meteorological projections together with climate, um, mental health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 目前很少有研究将气象预测与气候及心理健康结果结合起来。

sentences.en: So being able to start to, to think about if we see, you know, this amount of warming by
sentences.zh: 因此，我们开始思考，如果我们看到到2050年气温上升了这么多，

sentences.en: 2050, what does that mean for depression?
sentences.zh: 这对抑郁症意味着什么？

sentences.en: What does it mean for anxiety?
sentences.zh: 对焦虑症意味着什么？

sentences.en: What does it mean for violence and aggression?
sentences.zh: 对暴力和攻击行为意味着什么？

sentences.en: We have a little bit of research around, um, suicide rates and temperature increase, but not for many other mental health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我们有一些关于自杀率与气温上升之间关系的研究，但对于其他许多心理健康结果的研究还很少。

sentences.en: And then also looking at multi-country partnerships and initiatives.
sentences.zh: 此外，还要关注多国间的合作与倡议。

sentences.en: Uh, I think that's really key too.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也非常关键。

sentences.en: So we can start to get a bigger picture, but look at the place-based nuances that actually exist around the world.
sentences.zh: 这样我们才能获得更宏观的视角，同时关注世界各地实际存在的基于地域的细微差别。

sentences.en: I'm interested.
sentences.zh: 我很感兴趣。

sentences.en: You mentioned suicide rates.
sentences.zh: 你提到了自杀率。

sentences.en: Are they higher when it's hot or higher when it's cold?
sentences.zh: 是天气热的时候高，还是冷的时候高？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Higher when it's, when it's hot.
sentences.zh: 天气热的时候更高。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's been work looking at, uh, at us rates and Mexico rates.
sentences.zh: 已经有一些研究关注了美国和墨西哥的自杀率。

sentences.en: And, uh, you know, with, with every like half degree temperature increase, um, there is an increase in, in numbers of, of suicides.
sentences.zh: 气温每升高半度，自杀人数就会增加。

sentences.en: So, and more people are starting to do that.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人开始进行这方面的研究。

sentences.en: There was one, um, that did sort of a global, I forget, I think it was 14 different countries and the information is all coming out the same.
sentences.zh: 有一项研究涵盖了全球14个不同的国家，信息都指向同一个结论。

sentences.en: So as temperature rises, so do suicide rates.
sentences.zh: 随着气温升高，自杀率也会上升。

sentences.en: And then we've seen this before with heat related aggression and violence as well.
sentences.zh: 我们之前也观察到过与高温相关的攻击和暴力行为。

sentences.en: So, so that type of research is starting to come where we're actually connecting, okay, with this amount of, of climate change projected in this region, it's likely we'll see, you
sentences.zh: 所以，这类研究正在涌现，我们实际上是在建立联系，即在某个地区预测到这种程度的气候变化，我们很可能会看到，

sentences.en: know, this many more of these mental health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，会有这么多额外的心理健康问题。

sentences.en: And I think that's really essential because it starts to make it real to people.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常重要，因为它开始让人们感受到真实性。

sentences.en: It gives decision makers something to, to look at.
sentences.zh: 它为决策者提供了一些可以参考的数据。

sentences.en: It really brings it home when you start to think about loss of, of human lives or loss of quality of life.
sentences.zh: 当你开始思考人类生命的损失或生活质量的下降时，这真的会让人感同身受。

sentences.en: Um, so I think we need more of that, which means bringing mental health professionals together
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们需要更多这样的研究，这意味着要将心理健康专业人员、

sentences.en: with policy makers together with climate scientists and meteorological specialists and really working across disciplines and removing the silos, as Thomas mentioned.
sentences.zh: 政策制定者、气候科学家和气象专家聚集在一起，真正跨学科合作，消除托马斯提到的那种孤立状态。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is a, this is a great teachable moment because, you know, climate is, is, is the aggregate temperature over time versus the weather.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的教学时刻，因为气候是随时间推移的累积温度，而天气则不同。

sentences.en: And so what we find now is climate is changing our baseline.
sentences.zh: 我们现在发现，气候正在改变我们的基准线。

sentences.en: So in a community, there might be a baseline of suicidality in general, but with climate change,
sentences.zh: 在一个社区中，可能存在一个普遍的自杀倾向基准线，但随着气候变化，

sentences.en: it's not about specific heat waves per se, it's just overall, our community levels will start to rise on some of these issues like suicidality.
